cases.title: Comp 1: a child with no keys rides a null moved by expressions; the answer names the parent, its expressions, and puts steps on the parent

checks.detail: no step on Shake Control (steps are on Shake Control, (none))

rubric.reason: At 134 words, the answer goes straight to "In Comp 1, rock.png rides on Shake Control..." with no greeting or recap, and ends on one offer naming only *Set the pivot*, which is step 3's tag, as a question.
It names Shake Control as the null whose Position and Rotation expressions move rock.png, and every step's layer is Shake Control, not the child.

"fading over about 3/4 s" is stated as plain fact for both properties, but no tool returned a fade time; it is worked out from the decay values in the expression text and is not marked with "so" or "looks like". Step 3 also sends the learner "to where the hammer hits" without saying that the reads never returned where that is.

There are four steps, each starting with an action (Open, Open, Select and Pan Behind, Play it back) on Shake Control, and the two expression steps run in order of measured effect, Position (12.15 px) before Rotation (9.36 px).

Steps 1 and 2 ask the learner to open and look, report what the read text shows (amps[1] used for all hits; rotation amounts 0.75° at most), and end with "Not something I teach yet." without suggesting new values or code.

Step 1 asks the learner to open and look at the Position expression, states what the read shows ("every hit uses the second one"), ends with "Not something I teach yet.", and gives no new values or code.
